children: Starlink and other satellite operators await security approval as the government reviews operational and regulatory requirements for services

The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) is examining security-related issues concerning satellite communication services in India, Minister of State for Communications Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani said on Thursday, as satcom companies await final clearances to begin operations.

Speaking on the sidelines of India Mobile Congress 2026, Pemmasani said the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has issued licences and provisional spectrum to all satcom companies. He said the remaining process is pending with the MHA for security clearance.

Pemmasani said the issue is not related to any particular company and that the companies would receive the required clearance once the security process is completed. His remarks come as satellite communication companies prepare to enter the Indian market.

The development comes a day after SpaceX founder Elon Musk alleged that certain oligarchs were blocking his company’s satellite communication services in India to protect their monopoly. Musk made the allegation while responding to a post on X about the absence of mobile coverage in more than 11,000 villages.

Musk claimed that Starlink could provide connectivity to people who currently lack access to mobile services or cannot afford existing prices. He also alleged that the company was being prevented from offering services in India despite its potential to expand high-speed internet access.

Musk separately denied allegations that Starlink services had been used by militants in Manipur. He said Starlink beams are switched off over India and therefore rejected claims that the service had been used by anyone in the country.
His comments came as India Mobile Congress 2026 began, bringing renewed attention to the regulatory and security requirements governing satellite communication services in India.

A senior SpaceX official said on Wednesday that the company’s satellite communication arm is ready to begin services in India, subject to the necessary approvals. Speaking at India Mobile Congress 2026, Starlink Business Operations Vice President Lauren Dreyer said the company had already invested in infrastructure for the Indian market.

Dreyer said Starlink had built its operations specifically for India while taking into account the country’s security requirements and regulations. She said the company had established controls across its operations and would keep Indian user data within India.

According to Dreyer, Starlink has established 20 gateway sites across India with hundreds of antennas as part of its ground infrastructure. She said the company had already established the operations required to serve the Indian market.

Indian telecom operators have also indicated that clearances remain part of the process for satellite communication services. Bharti Airtel, Reliance Jio and Vodafone Idea did not react to Musk’s allegations regarding Starlink’s entry into India.

Bharti Airtel founder Sunil Bharti Mittal said his company is also awaiting clearance. Reliance Jio Chairman Akash Ambani said he had not seen Musk’s comments and therefore could not share his view on the matter.

The developments highlight the importance of security clearance in the rollout of satcom services in India, even as companies have secured licences, provisional spectrum and invested in the infrastructure required for commercial operations.
